title: Do the last three digits decide for eight?
description: Three statements about the last three digits and eight are tested on three numbers. The thousands are whole eights, so all three statements hold, and Keeko's doubt about a number ending in three zeros is broken.
teaching_notes: One idea: because a thousand is a whole number of eights, the last three digits alone decide, both ways. Watch for students who think a number ending in zeros cannot be divisible by eight.

source: Consider these statements: 1. Only the last three digits matter when deciding if a given number is divisible by 8. 2. If the number formed by the last three digits is divisible by 8, then the original number is divisible by 8. 3. If the original number is divisible by 8, then the number formed by the last three digits is divisible by 8. Do you agree? Why or why not?
video_script.why: The child splits a number into thousands and the last three digits, sees that the thousands are whole eights, and tests each statement on a number.
video_script.substitution: Split each number into thousands and the last three digits, then count each part in eights.
video_script.anchor: three statement cards, with a number card beside each: 8576, 7648 and 5024
video_script.wrong_answer: five thousand is not divisible by eight
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko says five thousand is not divisible by eight, because its last three digits are all zeros. Zero is zero eights, which is a whole number of eights, and five thousand is six hundred and twenty five eights, so the bubble is struck through.
video_script.payoff_line: Yes, all three statements are true

final_answer.value: Yes, all three are true. Examples: 8576, 7648, 5024
final_answer.spoken: yes, all three statements are true, for example eight thousand five hundred and seventy six, seven thousand six hundred and forty eight and five thousand and twenty four

hold_back: Answer: Yes, all three are true. Examples: 8576, 7648, 5024
maths_rules: 1000 = 125 x 8, so the thousands part of any number is a whole number of eights
so only the last three digits can leave something over, and statement 1 is true
the last three digits 024 make 24 = 3 x 8
000 = 0 x 8, so a number ending in three zeros is a whole number of eights
video_script.design: One idea: the thousands are whole eights, so the last three digits decide, both ways. Assumes the count in eights and the split into thousands. Wrong idea: a number ending in zeros cannot be divisible by eight. The statement cards stay on the board to the end.

<bookmark mark='rest'/>Take them away, and the last three digits, six hundred and forty eight, are eighty one eights.

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks five thousand is not divisible by eight.
<bookmark mark='why'/>The reason is that its last three digits are all zeros.
<bookmark mark='zero'/>But zero eights is a whole number of eights. Five thousand is six hundred and twenty five eights.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>Zeros at the end leave nothing over, so eight divides the number.
